summary: The v62 pass-wall Xorn can swap with its tame ghost on an obstructed square, and the ghost can follow through the closed doorway. C hack.c:domove_core() has no destination-terrain refusal; test_move() admits Passes_walls movement, and mon.c:mfndpos() sets thrudoor for ALLOW_WALL. JavaScript now admits those source-approved branches. When the hero later strikes the trapped door, C lock.c:doorlock() calls monmove.c:mb_trapped() for the resident ghost; JavaScript now calls its existing port, preserving the explosion message, damage, stun, and RNG. The admitted v62 replay matches all 689 screens, 3,223 RNG calls, and 689 cursors.

source.branch: hack.c:domove_core() reaches test_move(), which allows an obstructed destination for Passes_walls && may_passwall(), then runs do_attack() and domove_swap_with_pet() for a safe monster without rejecting the destination terrain. During the elapsed turn, mon.c:mfndpos() sets thrudoor when ALLOW_WALL is present, so the wall-walking ghost can enter a closed doorway; monmove.c:postmov() skips the ordinary door-opening path for passwall monsters. Later zap.c:bhit() calls lock.c:doorlock() for WAN_STRIKING; a trapped door with a monster at its square becomes D_NODOOR and calls monmove.c:mb_trapped().
callers: cmd.c zap command -> zap.c:bhit() -> lock.c:doorlock() -> monmove.c:mb_trapped().
dependencies: hack.c:test_move() admits obstructed movement when Passes_walls && may_passwall().
uhitm.c:do_attack() spends the source-ordered safe-monster draw before domove_core() swaps the pet.
mon.c:mfndpos() sets thrudoor for ALLOW_WALL and admits closed-door squares; monmove.c:postmov() skips door opening for passwall monsters.
dungeon.c:u_on_newpos() and hack.c:spoteffects() run after the successful hero swap.
lock.c:doorlock() discards mb_trapped()'s return value but relies on its message, RNG, damage, stun, death, and trap-learning effects. js/monmove.js already implements mb_trapped().

evidence: The original v62 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/accepted-ef4963eb5ba2f7992cc8c6d92bd1ace9fb796678-v62.json recorded 637/689 screens, 3150/3223 RNG calls, and 637/689 cursors, stopping at segment 0 step 637 on the unsupported safe-monster special-terrain preflight.
The saved worker replay after the fix at .cache/v62/replay-result.json reports a strict match: 689/689 screens, 3223/3223 RNG calls, 689/689 cursors, and zero animation frames on both sides.

The first source defect was js/hack.js:requireOrdinarySafeMonsterSwap(), which admitted only ROOM, CORR, furniture, or an empty door before do_attack(). C hack.c:test_move():1011-1018 admits an obstructed destination when Passes_walls && may_passwall(); hack.c:2922-2934 performs the safe-monster swap and u_on_newpos() without a terrain-type gate.

The elapsed-turn follow-up was js/unported_monster_actions.js:admitSimpleDestinationAndRegion(). C mon.c:2140-2222 derives thrudoor from ALLOW_WALL and lets that monster enter a closed door; monmove.c:1540-1590 skips door opening when the monster passes walls. JavaScript now admits pass-wall doors for this planner path.

The later step 660 RNG and screen mismatch was js/lock.js:doorlock() recording note_unported('trap.c mb_trapped') instead of calling the existing js/monmove.js:mb_trapped(). C lock.c:1201-1220 clears a trapped closed door and calls monmove.c:mb_trapped() for a monster at the square; the JS call now preserves its RNG and state/output effects.

Focused coverage in scripts/hack.test.mjs exercises the pass-wall safe-pet preflight and test_move() branch. scripts/lock.test.mjs checks door destruction, the discarded helper result, the explosion message, stun, HP loss, and rnd(15) ordering. The admitted v62 replay exercises the complete production path through both later branches.
